land.text: the Eastern Province (the Banda Oriental) and the provinces west of the Uruguay that left Buenos Aires in 1815

predecessors.note: The page: 'In 1814 he organized the Unión de los Pueblos Libres ... and in 1815 declared the Liga Federal.'

land.text: Entre Ríos, Corrientes, Misiones, Santa Fe and Córdoba: 'the Federal League effectively came to an end as a separate political entity' at Cepeda

successors.note: Cliopatria's 1820 Río de la Plata shape covers them again; Ramírez's Republic of Entre Ríos (Entre Ríos and Corrientes) ran from 29 September 1820 to September-October 1821 (Republic of Entre Ríos page; dossier republic-of-entre-rios).

land.text: the Eastern Province, 'fully captured by Portuguese Brazil' in 1820 and 'annexed by Portugal to its Brazilian dependences in 1821'

capitals.name: Purificación (Paysandú area)
capitals.note: The page: 'its leadership was based on Purificación and the Eastern Bank of the Uruguay River'. It gives no coordinates; those are the gazetteer's for Paysandú, the nearest listed town. After the Portuguese took Montevideo (20 January 1817) the page names no seat; Artigas retreated to Entre Ríos only at the end.

rulers.name: José Gervasio Artigas
rulers.title: Protector of the Free Peoples
rulers.note: 'In 1814 he organized the Unión de los Pueblos Libres, of which he was declared Protector'; after the defeat he withdrew to Entre Ríos and then to Paraguay, 'where he settled as an exile until his death'.

correction.text: the Eastern Bank without western Rio Grande do Sul (the Missions Portuguese since 1801)

keyframe_review.note: 288,874 km2 for 1814: Uruguay (94 percent) plus 131,761 km2 of western Rio Grande do Sul (521 cells). The Misiones Orientales page says the Missions were 'definitively ceded to Portugal in the Treaty of Badajoz (1801)' and it 'became part of Brazil' in 1822; no page opened shows League control east of the Uruguay River in Rio Grande do Sul (confidence 2: the page covers the Missions, not the whole slice). The Eastern Bank part stands: the page puts the League's leadership on 'Purificación and the Eastern Bank of the Uruguay River'; Montevideo itself was the United Provinces' from 23 June 1814 (rio-de-la-plata ledger).

correction.text: the League's provinces without western Rio Grande do Sul; the Portuguese occupation of Montevideo from 1817 is in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 604,813 km2 for 1815-1819: the Eastern Province, Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones, 62 percent of Santa Fe and 24 percent of Córdoba, plus the same 131,761 km2 of Rio Grande do Sul, removed here as in 1814. The page's member list ('Córdoba (with La Rioja), Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones, the Eastern Province, and Santa Fe') is matched; Cliopatria shares Córdoba and Santa Fe with the United Provinces and the page gives no join dates, so that split stands. Portugal invaded in August 1816 and took Montevideo on 20 January 1817 ('the struggle continued for three long years in the countryside'), which the shape ignores; the ledger carries it (Montevideo lost 1817, the Eastern Province 1820).

region.text: the Eastern Bank of the Uruguay River, where the leadership was based

ledger.note: 1814: Artigas organises the Union of the Free Peoples. 'In 1814 he organized the Unión de los Pueblos Libres (Union of the Free Peoples), of which he was declared Protector.' The page gives the Eastern Bank as the leadership's base but no boundary; the core is read as the Eastern Province.

region.text: Córdoba (with La Rioja), Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones and Santa Fe

ledger.note: 1815: Córdoba, Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones and Santa Fe join the League. 'in 1815 declared the Liga Federal'; the original members are Córdoba (with La Rioja), Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones, the Eastern Province and Santa Fe. No join dates on the page.

10 January 1815: Guayabos brings the Eastern Bank into the League. 'The federal victory at Guayabos on 10 January 1815 brought the Eastern Bank into the Federal League.' Montevideo, held by Buenos Aires since 23 June 1814, is included.
August 1816: Portugal invades the Eastern Province. 'in August, 1816 the latter invaded the Eastern Province' (the Portuguese Crown, from Brazil).

20 January 1817: the Portuguese take Montevideo. 'took Montevideo on January 20, 1817'; 'the struggle continued for three long years in the countryside'. Occupied, not yet annexed; the annexation as a Brazilian dependency was in 1821.

1820: the Eastern Bank falls to Portuguese Brazil. 'In 1820, the Eastern Bank was fully captured by Portuguese Brazil'; Artigas 'finally retreated to Entre Ríos Province, across the Uruguay River' (Federal League page); the Federal League page adds 'annexed by Portugal to its Brazilian dependences in 1821'.
1820: the fighting for the Eastern Province ends with its capture ('fully captured by Portuguese Brazil'); the League's last army retreats across the Uruguay.

region.text: Córdoba (with La Rioja), Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Misiones and Santa Fe

ledger.note: 1820: the provinces west of the Uruguay go back to the United Provinces' outline. The Federal armies of Ramírez and López defeated 'a diminished Supreme Directorship army at the Battle of Cepeda' and signed the Treaty of Pilar with Buenos Aires, which Artigas refused; 'the Federal League effectively came to an end as a separate political entity'. The Cepeda page dates the battle 1 February 1820 and Ramírez's Republic of Entre Ríos 29 September 1820.

1820: the Federal League ends. 'the Federal League effectively came to an end as a separate political entity'; Artigas 'withdrew to Paraguay, where he settled as an exile until his death'. Cliopatria's last shape is 1819.

wars.name: Battle of Guayabos
wars.outcome: Federal victory at Guayabos on 10 January 1815 brought the Eastern Bank into the League.

wars.name: Portuguese invasion of the Eastern Province
wars.outcome: Portugal invaded in August 1816, took Montevideo on 20 January 1817 and 'fully captured' the Eastern Bank in 1820; annexed as a Brazilian dependency in 1821.
wars.note: The page names no battle (Tacuarembó is not on it).

wars.name: Battle of Cepeda (1820)
wars.outcome: The Federal armies of Ramírez and López defeated the national government; the Treaty of Pilar (23 February 1820) was refused by Artigas; the League ended.

certainty.note: The League's frontiers are provincial and approximate; the Brazilian frontier on the Eastern Bank was not settled by any treaty the pages give.

sources.title: Federal League (1815-1820)
sources.note: Members, leadership, Portuguese invasion 1816-1821, Cepeda, Artigas's exile; no area or Guayabos date.

sources.title: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
sources.note: Guayabos 10 January 1815; Eastern Bank 'fully captured by Portuguese Brazil' in 1820.

sources.title: Misiones Orientales
sources.note: Portuguese since the Treaty of Badajoz (1801); check on the Rio Grande do Sul slice.

sources.title: Battle of Cepeda (1820)
sources.note: 1 February 1820 and the Republic of Entre Ríos.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Federal League' rows (1814 and 1815-1819) hold the Eastern Bank plus 131,761 km2 of western Rio Grande do Sul, for which the Misiones Orientales page has the Missions Portuguese from 1801 and no page opened shows League control east of the Uruguay River; both verdicts remove it (confidence 2). Portugal's occupation of Montevideo (20 January 1817) and the 'three long years' in the countryside are not in the shapes, which keep all of Uruguay to 1819; the ledger carries it (contest 1816-1820, Montevideo lost 1817). The pages give no area for the League and no join dates for its provinces. The League's end is 1820 (the page's title and Cepeda), a year after Cliopatria's last shape (1819); the land west of the Uruguay returns to the Río de la Plata dossier in 1820. The Battle of Tacuarembó, the Congress of Oriente and Arroyo de la China are not on the page. Ramírez's Republic of Entre Ríos (29 September 1820 - 1821) has its own dossier (republic-of-entre-rios); its infobox lists the Liga Federal as its predecessor.
